record.original_question: If A and B are approximately amenable Banach algebras, must their projective tensor product A \hat{\otimes} B be approximately amenable? Likewise, if A and B are pseudo-amenable Banach algebras, must A \hat{\otimes} B be pseudo-amenable?

evidence.quote: Definition 1.2. A Banach algebra A is called (resp. boundedly, sequentially, uniformly or weak* ) approximately amenable if every continuous derivation D: A -> X* is (resp. boundedly, sequentially, uniformly or weak* ) approximately inner for each Banach A-bimodule X.

Definition 1.3. A Banach algebra A is called pseudo-amenable (briefly, ps. a.) if it has an approximate diagonal, i.e. if there is a net (ui) subset A\u2297A\u0302 such that aui - uia -> 0 and \u03c0(ui)a -> a for all a in A.
Question 7. Is A\u2297B\u0302 approximately amenable (resp. pseudo-amenable) if both A and B are?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let A and B be Banach algebras over the complex field, and let A ⊗̂ B denote their projective tensor product (which is again a Banach algebra under the canonical multiplication (a₁⊗b₁)(a₂⊗b₂)=a₁a₂⊗b₁b₂ extended by continuity).

Recall the following definitions. A Banach algebra A is approximately amenable if for every Banach A-bimodule X, every continuous derivation D : A → X* is approximately inner, i.e., there exists a net (φ_i) ⊂ X* such that D(a) = lim_i (a·φ_i − φ_i·a) for every a ∈ A. A Banach algebra A is pseudo-amenable if it admits an approximate diagonal, i.e., a net (u_i) ⊂ A ⊗̂ A such that a·u_i − u_i·a → 0 and π(u_i)a → a for every a ∈ A, where π : A ⊗̂ A → A is the multiplication map.

Questions:
(i) If A and B are both approximately amenable, must A ⊗̂ B be approximately amenable?
(ii) If A and B are both pseudo-amenable, must A ⊗̂ B be pseudo-amenable?
artifact.status_search_result: A 2017 paper by Ghahramani and Loy ("Approximate amenability of tensor products of Banach algebras", J. Math. Anal. Appl.) addresses this question, providing positive results under additional hypotheses (notably presence of bounded approximate identities) and showing that in general the hereditary behavior under projective tensor products fails for approximate amenability, in contrast with classical amenability. The full general questions, especially the pseudo-amenable case, do not appear to have been completely settled.

status_evidence.title: Approximate amenability of tensor products of Banach algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates when approximate amenability of A and B implies (or is implied by) that of A⊗̂B; positive results under bounded approximate identity hypotheses.
status_evidence.claim: The question has been partially addressed: positive results hold under additional hypotheses, while in general hereditary properties differ from those for classical amenability.

status_evidence.title: Approximate semi-amenability of Banach algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses approximate amenability and related notions for Banach algebras and their tensor products.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature continues to study tensor product behavior of approximate amenability variants, indicating not all cases are resolved.
